Bytes from +0x002E onward read as zero in the runtime dump because relative_offset (0x13D1) + 128 (0x80) = 0x1451 exceeds this descriptor's own loaded code_size (0x13FF) by 0x52 bytes -- the fixed 128-byte dump window reads past the end of the descriptor's loaded buffer into unloaded/zero memory, while retail GAME.OVR simply continues into the next function's bytes at that contiguous file offset. This is a dump-window-boundary artifact of the trace methodology for short functions sitting near the tail of their descriptor, not evidence that the cluster's own structural correlation is wrong -- but per this evidence file's schema it is honestly recorded as a byte mismatch (not silently reclassified as confirmed), since the methodology only claims byte-identity across the full fixed dump window, not a variable-length function-body-only compare. See docs/engine/research/coab-symbol-runtime-bytematch-round3.md. |

## Claim Boundary

A `symbols` entry means a native CoAB CS:IP trace (BPINT 21 42 seek-capture + post-read breakpoint + `D segment:offset` dump, see docs/engine/research/coab-symbol-runtime-bytematch.md and its round-2 sibling) reached that exact retail_file_offset at a resolved runtime segment during ordinary silent startup and found the resident bytes byte-identical to retail GAME.OVR, reproduced at least twice. It does NOT mean CS:IP was ever observed executing inside that function during real gameplay -- only that the loaded bytes are correct post-load, the same limitation already recorded for Gateway's descriptor-9 doc. `unconfirmed` candidates are statically promoted (some title's own oracle/dispatch evidence reaches them) but have no runtime trace attempt yet, or the attempt could not reach them without a save file -- they are not assumed correct. `rejected` candidates had a runtime trace attempt that produced a genuine byte mismatch; this is retained as negative evidence, never silently dropped. `unnamed_structural_confirmations` (round 3, see docs/engine/research/coab-symbol-runtime-bytematch-round3.md) is a DIFFERENT claim: these are the 25 promoted-but-UNNAMED (`sub_XXXXX` placeholder) clusters, byte-matched the same way, but the result only confirms/rejects the STATIC STRUCTURAL correlation that promoted the cluster -- it never assigns or implies a semantic name, and these entries never appear in `symbols`.
